transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO, Zenith), Aisha Malik (Lead ML Eng), Tom Reyes (DevOps), Sofia Lin (Security)

Summary / Agenda: quick intros, current stack & constraints, integration patterns (SDKs vs gateway), LangChain/LlamaIndex support, rate limiting and quotas, observability/tracing hooks, security/compliance Qs, next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Olivia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Olivia from Redwood, and with me is Marco, our SE. Quick intros?
[00:12] Daniel: Hi, Daniel Park, CTO at Zenith. We've got Aisha and Tom and Sofia on the line.
[00:18] Aisha: Hi all.
[00:20] Marco: Great. Our goal today is to understand your integration surface and constraints — SDKs, LLM toolkits like Lang Chain and LlamaIndex, whether you want a gateway/proxy pattern or direct SDK calls, and observability hooks.
[00:32] Tom: We mainly care about latency and audit logs. We're a payments company so data residency and retention matter.
[00:38] Olivia: Got it. High level — Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Each has tradeoffs for latency/cost and control. For integrations you can either call Redwood SDKs directly from your app, or run a lightweight gateway that centralizes auth, rate-limiting, and caching.
[00:54] Daniel: Could you expand on the gateway pattern? Our infra team prefers a single ingress point so we can manage quotas and observability.
[01:02] Marco: Absolutely. We often suggest a FastAPI/Express gateway that uses Redwood SDK/server-side client to call the API. Benefits: centralized rate-limit enforcement, single place for request/response transformation, and you can attach application-level tracing. We have an example repo.
[01:20] Aisha: How does that differ from running a local model or self-hosting? Latency is critical — p50 under 100ms for short prompts.
[01:28] Marco: Self-hosting can reduce hop latency if you colocate models on-prem, but you trade off operational complexity and model updates. Dedicated pools give you reserved GPUs with predictable throughput and lower variance versus Hosted. For sub-100ms, sequence length and model size matter — we can recommend smaller quantized variants.
[01:45] Sofia: Security questions — KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO. Do you support SAML?
[01:51] Olivia: Yes, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management in Private deployments. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and customer-managed KMS as an option for enterprise tiers. Audit logs are available with retention tiers. We'll share SOC2 and compliance pack.
[02:07] Tom: About rate limits and quotas — can we set per-team quotas and burst allowances?
[02:13] Marco: Yes, per-API-key quotas, per-route quotas, and we support burst windows. On Dedicated/Private you can configure autoscaling/burst capacity policies and have higher quota ceilings. For Hosted API there's standard tiered quotas but enterprise plans allow custom SLAs.
[02:30] Daniel: Integration with LangChain and LlamaIndex — do you have first-class connectors?
[02:36] Marco: We have SDKs and several examples. LangChain works via our LLM wrapper, some community adapters exist, and we provide sample code. LlamaIndex is sometimes transcribed as "LamaIndex" in notes, but we mean LlamaIndex — we have a connector pattern for embeddings + vector stores. We'll send snippets.
[02:58] Aisha: Any specifics on streaming vs non-streaming for tool-assisted workflows? We use streaming for UI responsiveness.
[03:05] Marco: We support streaming responses over HTTP/WS. For streaming plus function/tool-calls, we recommend keeping the gateway connection open and forwarding chunks. Streaming slightly increases connection overhead but reduces perceived latency in UI.
[03:20] Daniel: Observability — tracing, token-level cost, and per-route dashboards. How do we instrument?
[03:26] Olivia: We expose tracing hooks and an open telemetry exporter — you can tag requests with correlation IDs and get token-level cost breakdowns in the Console. We also provide per-model/per-route dashboards and exportable logs for SIEM.
[03:40] Tom: For the gateway, would we attach OpenTelemetry spans?
[03:44] Marco: Exactly. Our SDKs propagate trace context and we have middleware for common frameworks.
[03:50] Aisha: Regarding embeddings and vector DBs — do you handle vectorization at inference or in a separate embeddings pipeline? We want to keep embedding generation auditable.
[03:58] Marco: Embeddings are separate endpoints; you can call them via the same SDK and persist vectors to your store. For Private deployments, you can run the embeddings worker locally for data residency.
[04:12] Sofia: Compliance: retention windows and ability to disable retention for certain model calls?
[04:17] Olivia: We provide configurable retention policies and a do-not-store flag for sensitive requests. For Private, logs and data stay in customer VPC. Hosted offers enterprise retention controls and DSR support.
[04:30] Daniel: Pricing — curious about unit economics for Dedicated vs Hosted for our volume. We'll want a cost model.
[04:36] Olivia: We'll share a benchmark/cost worksheet tailored to your QPS and prompt lengths — Marco will run a quick profile recommendation and suggested quantized model families.
[04:46] Aisha: Do you have rate limiting examples for per-customer routing? We sometimes route by customer tier — gold/silver/free.
[04:53] Marco: Yes, routing policies support tier-based routing, by header or token. You can route to cheaper quantized variants for lower tiers and reserve higher-performance variants for SLAs.
[05:06] Tom: Are there known gotchas with TLS and proxying through our API gateway? We terminate TLS at the edge.
[05:12] Marco: Most customers terminate TLS at their edge and then use mTLS to Redwood private endpoints for Private deployments. For Hosted, mutual TLS is supported for enterprise. We'll include a network diagram in the docs.
[05:26] Daniel: We need to proof a POC. What's a minimal POC?
[05:30] Olivia: Typical POC: 2–4 week trial, sample traffic replayed against Dedicated or Hosted, run 5–10 prompt templates + embeddings, measure latency/cost and quality. We can provide a harness and run comparative runs.
[05:45] Aisha: Timeline — we aim to select a solution by end of year and pilot in Q1.
[05:50] Olivia: Sounds doable. Next up we'll send a sample repo with LangChain and LlamaIndex snippets and a FastAPI gateway example, plus security docs and a benchmarking worksheet.
[06:00] Sofia: We'll want a security deep-dive and maybe a dedicated trial environment.
[06:04] Olivia: We'll coordinate — Marco will own the benchmark materials and I'll get the security team involved.
[06:10] Daniel: Great, thanks.

(Throughout: occasional transcription artifacts — "LamaIndex" for LlamaIndex, "Lang Chain" spaced, some names slightly garbled in auto notes.)

Recap & agreed next steps:
- Redwood to send SDK + LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a sample FastAPI gateway repo.
- Marco to share performance benchmark spreadsheet and suggested model/quant settings.
- Redwood to provide SOC2/compliance pack and KMS integration guidance.
- Customer to share QPS targets and compliance checklist; provision VPC details if pursuing Private trial.

End of transcript.
